title: Rowing vs Running: Which Builds Full-Body Fitness?
summary: Rowing vs running for full-body conditioning: muscle recruitment, injury risk, bone density and strength compared, plus how to combine both.
body_text: Rowing vs. Running for Full-Body Conditioning Both build serious fitness. They just load very different amounts of you. For full-body conditioning specifically, rowing wins. A rowing stroke recruits over 85% of your muscles across nine major muscle groups, while running is predominantly a lower-body activity with the upper body acting as a stabilizer rather than a worker. Rowing also lets you add resistance, so it trains strength endurance in a way running cannot. Running still beats rowing on two counts that matter: it builds bone density in your legs and hips because it is weight-bearing, and it is the more specific choice if running itself is your goal. The honest answer for most people is that rowing is the better single machine for whole-body conditioning, and running is the better supplement to it. In this article Which works more muscle? The conditioning scorecard Does rowing build real strength? Which is harder on your body? What running does better How to combine both FAQ Which works more muscle, rowing or running? Rowing, and not by a small margin. Indoor rowing recruits more than 85% of the muscles in your body across nine major muscle groups, according to British Rowing . The stroke breaks down to roughly 60% legs, 20% core and 20% arms, so every single repetition is a coordinated push, brace and pull. Your quads and glutes drive, your trunk transfers the force, and your lats, rhomboids and biceps finish it. Then you do it again, 25 times a minute. Running is a superb cardiovascular activity, but its muscular demand is concentrated below the waist: quads, hamstrings, glutes and calves, with the core stabilizing and the arms swinging for balance and rhythm. Your back and shoulders are along for the ride. That is not a criticism, it is just what the movement is, and it explains why runners so often need separate strength work to stay durable while rowers get a meaningful chunk of it built in. If you want the detail on which muscles rowing actually hits, we broke it down in what muscles a rowing machine works . The full-body conditioning scorecard Factor Rowing Running Muscle recruited 85%+, nine major groups Mainly lower body Upper body and back Loaded every stroke Postural only Adjustable resistance Yes, a true strength range No, only pace and incline Joint impact Low, no ground impact High, repeated loading Injury risk Lower, mostly form-related About 26% of recreational runners a year Bone density, legs and hips Limited, non weight-bearing Strong, weight-bearing Calories per minute High Slightly higher Learning curve Real technique to learn Almost none Does rowing actually build strength, or just endurance? This is where the comparison stops being close, because rowing has a lever running does not: resistance. When you run, your only intensity controls are pace and gradient. You cannot make each stride heavier. On a rower you can make every stroke heavier, which turns a cardio session into a strength-endurance session without changing machines. On an Aviron rower, levels 1 to 10 cover the cardio range and levels 11 to 16 add up to 100 lbs of magnetic resistance, which is genuinely loaded work for your legs, back and grip rather than just faster cardio. Guided programs add off-machine strength work, which is the piece runners usually have to bolt on separately. Be realistic about the ceiling: rowing will not build maximal strength the way heavy barbell work does, and nobody should claim otherwise. What it does is develop muscular endurance across almost your whole body at the same time as your aerobic base, which is precisely what "conditioning" means. For a fuller list of what that delivers, see 15 rowing machine benefits . Best for full-body conditioning Aviron Strong Rower Dual air and magnetic resistance with a dedicated strength range, plus guided programs that add off-machine work. Prefer to run? The Victory Treadmill runs the same library. 30-day risk-free home trial · Financing available See the Strong Rower → Which is harder on your body? Running, clearly, and the numbers are not subtle. Across a systematic review of studies covering more than 23,000 runners, the annual incidence of running-related injury in recreational runners was about 26% , and runners sustained roughly 7.7 injuries per 1,000 hours of running . The knee is the most commonly injured site at around a quarter of all injuries, followed by the foot and ankle and the lower leg. A cushioned deck reduces impact compared with pavement, but running is still weight-bearing by definition. Rowing removes ground impact entirely. Your feet never leave the footplate, so there is no landing force to absorb, which is why rowing is a standard recommendation for people with knee or hip complaints who still want hard cardio. It is not risk-free: the characteristic rowing injury is lower back pain, and it comes almost entirely from one error, opening your hips and swinging your torso back before your legs have finished driving. That is a technique problem with a technique fix, covered in correct rowing machine form . What does running do better than rowing? Two things, and a post that skipped them would not be worth reading. Bone density. This is running's real advantage. Because running is weight-bearing, the ground reaction forces and muscle strain it generates stimulate bone, and runners show greater bone mineral density throughout the lower limb than inactive people. Rowing sits between weight-bearing and non weight-bearing, and the evidence is more mixed: research on elite rowers found no significant difference in total bone density compared with controls, but a notable redistribution of bone mass from the lower limbs toward the trunk . If protecting hip and leg bone density is a priority, rowing alone is not the complete answer, and you should add weight-bearing work. Specificity. If your goal is to run a 10K, run. No amount of rowing makes you good at absorbing landing forces or holding running economy at pace. Rowing is excellent cross-training for runners precisely because it adds aerobic volume without adding impact, which is a different job from making you a better runner. We covered that trade in is the rowing machine good for runners . On calories, running holds a slight per-minute edge at matched effort, though the gap is smaller than most people assume and rowing lets you accumulate more total minutes without beating up your joints. The real numbers are in how many calories rowing burns and is rowing good for weight loss . How should you combine rowing and running? Stop treating it as a either-or. The two are close to complementary: rowing supplies upper-body and posterior-chain conditioning plus impact-free aerobic volume, and running supplies weight-bearing loading and running-specific fitness. A simple weekly split that works for general conditioning: two rowing sessions, one of them in the strength range, plus one or two runs. Row on the days after hard runs, because it lets you train aerobically while your joints recover. If you only ever want to own and use one machine, row, then add bodyweight or loaded lower-body work for bone health. Condition your whole body, not a quarter of it Games, classes and guided programs on a rower built for cardio and strength. Try it at home before you commit. Explore the Strong Rower → 30-day risk-free home trial. Free shipping, and no restocking or return shipping fees. Frequently asked questions Is rowing better than running? For full-body conditioning and joint safety, yes. Rowing recruits over 85% of your muscles and removes ground impact, and it lets you add resistance to train strength endurance. Running is better for building bone density in your legs and hips, and better if running itself is the goal. Neither is universally superior, but rowing is the stronger choice as a single all-round conditioning tool. What muscles does rowing work that running does not? Mainly your back and arms: lats, rhomboids, rear shoulders and biceps, all of which are loaded on every stroke. Rowing also loads your core far more actively, because your trunk has to transfer leg drive into the handle rather than simply staying upright. In running, the upper body stabilizes and swings but is never really under load. Does rowing burn more calories than running? Running burns slightly more per minute at an equivalent effort level, but the difference is smaller than most people expect. Because rowing is non-impact, many people can row longer and more frequently without soreness, so weekly totals often end up similar or better. Total consistent effort matters far more than per-minute rate. Is rowing or running better for weight loss? Whichever you will do consistently, because weight loss comes down to a sustained calorie deficit rather than machine choice. Rowing has a practical edge for many people: it is easier on the joints, so it is easier to keep doing four or five times a week for months, and it preserves more upper-body muscle while you lose fat. Can rowing replace running entirely? For general fitness and conditioning, yes. For bone health it is an incomplete replacement, because rowing is not fully weight-bearing, so pair it with walking, hiking or resistance training. And if you have a running goal, rowing supplements your training rather than substituting for it. Is rowing easier on your joints than running? Considerably. Your feet stay strapped to the footplate, so there is no landing impact at all, which is why rowing is routinely recommended for people managing knee, hip or ankle issues. The one caveat is your lower back, which stays healthy as long as you drive with your legs before opening your hips.

title: What Is an AI Finance Assistant? (And How Is It Different from an AI Agent?)
summary: An AI finance assistant answers questions about billing and revenue data. An AI agent takes action. Here's the real distinction, and which one your team should start with.
body_text: An AI finance assistant is software that answers questions about a company's financial or billing data in plain language, instead of requiring someone to build a report, write a query, or navigate a dashboard to get the same answer. Ask it why revenue dropped, what a specific customer's invoice history looks like, or how churn compares across segments, and it returns an answer grounded in the underlying records, not a general-knowledge guess. That's a narrower definition than most of what ranks for this term today. Search "AI financial assistant" and most of what comes back is personal finance: budgeting apps, a Medium post about someone's weekend project building a local assistant for their own spending, Intuit Assist helping consumers with taxes and cash flow. None of that is wrong, exactly, it's just a different problem than the one a finance or RevOps team at a company has. This piece is about the second thing, and about a distinction that gets blurred even within that world: the difference between an assistant and an agent. What an AI finance assistant actually does Three capabilities show up in every real implementation. It answers natural-language questions over structured financial data (MRR, invoices, subscriptions, usage events) instead of requiring a BI tool or a request to the data team. It shows its work: the records and calculations behind an answer should be inspectable, not just stated. And it stays inside a defined scope: a finance assistant, specifically, is usually read-only. It reports and explains. It doesn't change an invoice or cancel a subscription. That's a deliberate boundary, not a limitation someone forgot to lift. Assistant vs. agent: the distinction that actually matters An AI finance assistant answers questions. A finance AI agent takes multi-step action toward a goal. That's the core distinction, and it matters more than it sounds like it should, because most vendor marketing uses both terms to describe roughly the same confident-sounding chatbot. The line gets blurry in practice because every real agent implementation has an assistant-like component inside it. Before an agent can decide what to do, it usually has to ask itself something in natural language and retrieve an answer, which looks identical to what a pure assistant does. The difference isn't visible in any single interaction. It's visible in what happens after the answer: does a human read it and act, or does the system act on its own? This is also why content on "finance AI agent" tends to skew abstract (see AI Agents in Finance for what we found when we checked what's actually deployed versus what's described in enterprise consulting decks), while content on "AI finance assistant" skews toward personal budgeting tools that have nothing to do with a company's revenue operations. Neither side of the current search results really answers this comparison directly, which is a big part of why this confusion persists. Which one should a finance team actually want For most teams, the honest answer is: start with the assistant. A system that answers questions and shows its work is lower-risk, easier to trust, and easier to evaluate than one that's already taking action. The agent capabilities, scheduled reconciliation, autonomous anomaly flagging, become valuable once the assistant layer has proven the underlying data and reasoning are reliable enough to build on. That's the sequencing Lago's own Finance AI Assistant follows: read-only first, wider scope earned over time, not granted upfront. Where this fits into billing and revenue data Billing and revenue data is a particularly good fit for an AI finance assistant, because the underlying objects (subscriptions, invoices, usage events) are structured and well-defined. That's a big part of why Lago built one directly on top of billing data rather than as a general-purpose chat layer. Billing observability covers the metrics and alerting side of that same visibility problem. Key takeaways An AI finance assistant answers plain-language questions about financial and billing data, grounded in real records, and stays read-only by design in most serious implementations. An AI agent, by contrast, pursues a goal across multiple steps with less human input per step, and carries a higher risk profile because its worst-case outcome is an autonomous action based on a wrong inference rather than just an unhelpful answer. For most teams evaluating either, starting with assistant-level capabilities and earning agent-level autonomy over time is the lower-risk path. And most existing content on these terms is written for personal finance or enterprise abstraction, not for a company's finance or RevOps team, which is the gap this piece is meant to close.

title: Amazon EC2 R8i and R8i-Flex instances are now available in Canada West (Calgary) region
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon EC2 R8i and R8i-Flex instances are now available in Canada West (Calgary) region
body_text: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) R8i and R8i-flex instances are available in the Canada West (Calgary) region. These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The R8i and R8i-flex instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances. They deliver 20% higher performance than R7i instances, with even higher gains for specific workloads. They are up to 30% faster for PostgreSQL databases, up to 60% faster for NGINX web applications, and up to 40% faster for AI deep learning recommendation models compared to R7i. R8i-flex, our first memory-optimized Flex instances, are the easiest way to get price performance benefits for a majority of memory-intensive workloads. They offer the most common sizes, from large to 16xlarge, and are a great first choice for applications that don't fully utilize all compute resources. R8i instances are a great choice for all memory-intensive workloads, especially for workloads that need the largest instance sizes or continuous high CPU usage. R8i instances offer 13 sizes including 2 bare metal sizes and the new 96xlarge size for the largest applications. R8i instances are SAP-certified and deliver 142,100 aSAPS, the highest among all comparable machines in on-premises and cloud environments, delivering exceptional performance for mission-critical SAP workloads. To get started, sign in to the AWS Management Console . Customers can purchase these instances via Savings Plans, On-Demand instances, and Spot instances. For more information about the new R8i and R8i-flex instances visit the AWS News blog .

title: Why Bank Jago Transfer Failed: Common Causes and Fixes
summary: Is your Bank Jago transfer failing? Discover the most common reasons why Bank Jago transfers fail and how to fix them fast.
body_text: Banking You have bills to pay, someone waiting on a transfer, and then it happens: your Bank Jago transaction just… fails. No clear explanation, just a failed status staring back at you. Frustrating, right? The good news is that most Bank Jago transfer failures are totally fixable once you know what caused them. Let’s walk through the most common culprits and exactly what you can do about each one. List of Content Toggle Why Bank Jago Transfer Failed: The Big Picture Before panicking, know this: a failed transfer does not automatically mean something is seriously wrong. Bank Jago is a digital-first bank, which means it relies on a stable connection between your app, the banking system, and the destination bank. Any hiccup along that chain can trigger a failure. Here are the main reasons it happens. 1. Insufficient Account Balance This one sounds obvious, but it catches people off guard more often than you would think. If your balance does not cover the full transfer amount, the transaction will be rejected immediately. Double-check your available balance before trying again. Remember that your balance might look healthy, but a pending transaction from earlier could be temporarily holding some of those funds. 2. Incorrect Destination Account Details One wrong digit in the account number is all it takes. Bank Jago’s system verifies the destination account before processing, and if the number does not match a registered account, the transfer will not go through. Always copy and paste account numbers when possible, or triple-check manually. If you saved a beneficiary in the past, make sure the saved details are still up to date. 3. Exceeding the Daily Transfer Limit Bank Jago sets transaction limits, and if you have already sent a large amount earlier in the day, your next transfer might be blocked. This is a security feature, not a bug. Check your daily limit and your remaining allowance inside the Bank Jago app. If you genuinely need to send more, you may need to wait until the limit resets or contact Bank Jago support to discuss your options. 4. Unstable Internet Connection Because Bank Jago is a fully digital bank, a weak or dropping internet signal during a transfer can cause it to fail mid-process. This is especially common when switching between WiFi and mobile data. Try switching to a stronger network or a stable WiFi connection before attempting the transfer again. Avoid initiating transfers in areas with poor signal. 5. Bank Jago App Glitch or Outdated Version If the app itself has a bug or you are running an outdated version, certain features including transfers can break. Developers push updates regularly to fix exactly these kinds of issues. Head to the App Store or Google Play, check if a Bank Jago update is available, and install it. After updating, restart the app and try your transfer again. 6. Scheduled System Maintenance Banks routinely take their systems offline for maintenance, usually in the early hours of the morning. If your transfer fails late at night or very early in the morning, this could be the reason. Wait a short while and try again. Bank Jago often notifies users about maintenance windows through the app or their official social media channels, so it is worth checking those. 7. Destination Bank System Issues Sometimes the problem is not with Bank Jago at all. If the receiving bank is experiencing downtime or technical issues, your transfer can fail on the other end, even though everything on your side is perfectly fine. If this is the case, there is not much you can do except wait and try again later. You can also contact Bank Jago customer service to confirm whether the issue is on the receiving bank’s side. How to Fix a Failed Bank Jago Transfer Step by Step If your transfer has failed, do not just hit retry immediately. Follow these steps to actually solve the problem rather than triggering another failure. Check your balance. Make sure you have enough funds to cover the full amount you are trying to send. Verify the account number. Carefully re-read the destination account number. One wrong digit will cause a failure every time. Check your daily limit. Open the app settings or transaction history to see how much of your daily transfer limit you have already used. Test your internet connection. Switch networks if needed and confirm you have a stable connection before trying again. Update the Bank Jago app. If an update is available, install it. Outdated apps are a common but overlooked source of transaction errors. Wait and retry. If the issue seems related to maintenance or the destination bank, give it 15 to 30 minutes before trying again. Contact Bank Jago support. If none of the above steps resolve the issue, reach out to Bank Jago’s customer service directly. They can see error codes on the backend that you cannot access from the app. What Happens to Your Money After a Failed Transfer? One of the first questions people ask after a failed transfer is: where did my money go? This is a completely fair concern. In almost all cases, if a transfer fails, the funds are either never deducted in the first place or they are automatically returned to your Bank Jago account within a short period. Banks are required to reverse any deducted funds if the transaction does not complete successfully. That said, the timeline for a refund can vary. If the money was deducted but the transfer failed, it might take anywhere from a few minutes to a couple of business days to reappear in your balance, depending on where in the process the failure occurred. If the funds do not return within a reasonable timeframe, contact Bank Jago customer service immediately with your transaction reference number as proof. Tips to Avoid Bank Jago Transfer Failures in the Future Prevention is always easier than troubleshooting. Here are a few simple habits that will keep your Bank Jago transfers running smoothly. Always verify account details before confirming. Take an extra five seconds to read the number back before tapping send. Keep the app updated. Turn on automatic updates so you are always on the latest, most stable version. Transfer on a strong connection. Avoid sending money when your signal bars are low or you are switching networks. Monitor your daily limit. If you regularly send large amounts, be aware of your limit so you are never caught off guard. Avoid peak maintenance windows. Very late night or early morning transfers carry a slightly higher chance of hitting a maintenance window. Need to Send Money Internationally? Consider Transfez If your transfer needs involve sending money abroad, that adds another layer of complexity. Domestic transfer issues are one thing, but international transfers come with their own set of rules, conversion processes, and potential failure points. Transfez is a remittance service built specifically for international transfers from Indonesia. It is designed to make cross-border transactions more transparent and straightforward, which means fewer surprises and a smoother experience compared to routing international payments through a standard bank account. Worth exploring if you regularly send money overseas. Final Thoughts A failed Bank Jago transfer is annoying, but it is rarely a disaster. In most cases, the cause is something simple like a typo in the account number, a low balance, or a shaky internet connection. Work through the checklist above and you will likely solve the problem in minutes. And remember: your money is almost always safe. Failed transactions are built into banking systems with automatic safeguards to protect your funds. Stay calm, trace the cause, and you will have your transfer sorted out before you know it. Sending money to family studying, working, or traveling overseas? Transfez has you covered. Available on Android and iOS — download now! title: 5 Best Creams for Fungal Infections: Dermatologists Recommended
summary: Stop itching fast. Compare the 5 best dermatologist-recommended creams for fungal skin infections, key active ingredients, and prevention tips.
body_text: Ingredients to Look For Best Cream for Fungal Infections Tips to Prevent Fungal Recurrence How to Apply Anti-Fungal Cream? FAQs Fungal infections are one of the most common and persistent skin issues people face today. Caused by an overgrowth of microscopic organisms like yeasts and dermatophytes that thrive in warm, damp environments, these infections show up in everyday forms like athlete’s foot, ringworm, jock itch, and cutaneous candidiasis. Left unchecked, a minor patch of irritated skin can quickly spiral into relentless itching, burning, redness, and peeling. While the discomfort is real, relief is usually just a tube away. The key is knowing which active ingredient matches your specific symptom, whether that's targeting stubborn ringworm or soothing a sweaty skin fold. In this guide, we break down the top dermatologist-recommended antifungal creams, how they work, and exactly how to choose the right one to clear your skin for good. Ingredients That Actually Fight Fungal Infections Not all antifungal creams work the same way. Different active ingredients target fungi in unique ways, and picking the right one depends mostly on the specific issue you are dealing with. When you scan the back of the box, here are the main ingredients to look out for and why they matter: 1. Allylamines (Terbinafine, Naftifine) Allylamines are usually the first choice for common surface infections like athlete's foot, ringworm , and jock itch. How they work: They block a key enzyme that fungi rely on to build their protective outer walls, which ultimately breaks down the fungal cells. Why look for them: They actually kill the fungus rather than just slowing it down. Because of this, they tend to offer quicker relief and shorter treatment times, often clearing up mild infections in about one to two weeks. 2. Azoles (Clotrimazole, Miconazole, Ketoconazole) Azoles are friendly, versatile active ingredients found in many over-the-counter creams. How they work: They disrupt how the fungus produces ergosterol, a vital building block of its cell membrane. Without it, the membrane weakens and leaks. Why look for them: They work against a wide variety of issues, including both typical skin fungi and yeast infections like Candida (which often causes rashes in warm skin folds). Since they focus on stopping the fungus from growing and spreading, sticking to your daily routine is the secret to getting good results. 3. Polyenes (Nystatin) Nystatin is a more specialized ingredient that you will usually see suggested for specific yeast issues. How they work: It attaches directly to the fungal wall, opening up tiny pores that cause the cell to lose what it needs to survive. Why look for them: It is specifically tailored to tackle Candida yeast. It works well for chafed, moist skin folds, though it will not help with typical ringworm or athlete's foot. 4. Extra Support Ingredients (Tolnaftate, Zinc Oxide, Hydrocortisone) Tolnaftate: A reliable option that works well for treating an athlete's foot and keeping it from coming back. Zinc Oxide and Moisture Barriers: These help soothe raw or tender skin while the active medication goes to work underneath. Mild Hydrocortisone (1%): Sometimes added to calm intense itching and redness in the first few days. Note: Using a plain steroid cream on its own without an antifungal can actually make a fungal rash worse, so it is always best to stick to a combination formula or double-check with a professional first. Top 5 Anti-Fungal Creams Suggested by Skin Doctors Finding an effective solution for fungal, requires medical intervention and a proper understanding of the conditions. Here are some of the best creams for fungal infections that dermatologists often recommend for better relief. Product Name Key Ingredients Benefits Lulican Cream Luliconazole (1% w/w) Fast-acting, targeted treatment for dermatophyte infections (ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch); penetrates skin efficiently to relieve itching, redness, and inflammation. Sertazone Cream Sertaconazole Nitrate (2% w/w) Broad-spectrum treatment for athlete's foot, ringworm, jock itch, and candidiasis; disrupts fungal cell membranes to provide quick relief, support healing, and help prevent recurrence. Livafin CP Cream Amorolfine (0.25% w/w) Clinically proven and dermatologist-recommended for deep-penetrating, sustained protection against stubborn infections like ringworm and athlete's foot; gentle on skin for daily use. Ebernet Plus Cream Eberconazole (1% w/w) Prescription-strength formula targeting ringworm, athlete's foot, and jock itch; penetrates deeply for quick relief from redness, itching, and inflammation without causing irritation. Candidox Cream Ciclopirox Olamine (1% w/w) Prescription-strength treatment targeting a wide range of pathogens (ringworm, athlete's foot, fungal dermatitis); deep-penetrating, soothing base that relieves irritation and promotes healthy skin. 1. Lulican Cream Lulican (Luliconazole 1%) works rapidly against common skin fungi like ringworm, athlete’s foot, and jock itch. Its primary advantage is skin retention: it binds tightly to the outer layer of the skin, meaning it often requires a shorter overall duration of treatment (sometimes just 1 to 2 weeks of once-daily application) while keeping symptoms like itching and redness managed effectively. Who should avoid it: Anyone with a known allergy to luliconazole or imidazole-class antifungals should pass. Children under 12 years old (or under 2 for ringworm of the body) should generally avoid it unless a doctor explicitly prescribes it, as safety and efficacy data for pediatric use are limited. Pregnant or nursing women should consult a doctor first. 2. Sertazone Cream Sertazone (Sertaconazole Nitrate 2%) is a versatile, broad-spectrum solution. Beyond fighting ringworm and athlete's foot, it also tackles Candida yeast infections (candidiasis). It stands out because it offers dual benefit: direct antifungal action alongside mild anti-inflammatory properties, providing fast relief for angry, inflamed, or itching skin while lowering the risk of infection recurrence. Who should avoid it: Avoid if you have a hypersensitivity or allergic reaction to sertaconazole or other azole antifungals. It is not generally recommended for children under 12 years of age. Pregnant and breastfeeding individuals should avoid using it without clear medical guidance. 3. Livafin CP Cream Livafin (Amorolfine 0.25%) is well-regarded for its deep skin penetration and prolonged protective action. It alters the structure of the fungal membrane through a unique mechanism, making it a reliable pick for stubborn or lingering fungal skin infections that do not respond to basic treatments, all while remaining gentle on daily application. Who should avoid it: Individuals with known allergies to amorolfine or any of the inactive ingredients in the base. It is generally not recommended for children under 18 or for pregnant and lactating women due to a lack of safety clinical data for those groups. 4. Ebernet Plus Cream Ebernet Plus (Eberconazole 1%) is an advanced imidazole derivative that works remarkably well on inflamed or irritated skin. It is highly effective at clearing dermatophytes without causing secondary localized skin irritation, making it an excellent choice for individuals with sensitive skin who experience burning or stinging from other strong topical antifungals. Who should avoid it: Anyone who has had an allergic reaction to eberconazole or similar imidazole antifungals. Children (as safety is not established for pediatric patients) and pregnant/breastfeeding women should avoid using it without direct medical authorization. 5. Candidox Cream Candidox (Ciclopirox Olamine 1%) operates differently from traditional azoles, making it effective against a broad range of fungal pathogens, including fungus species that may have developed resistance to standard treatments. In addition to killing fungi, ciclopirox olamine possesses mild antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties, making it valuable when an infection is irritated or at risk of secondary bacterial growth. Who should avoid it: Individuals with a history of hypersensitivity to ciclopirox olamine. Avoid applying it to open, deep wounds or sensitive mucous membranes, and consult a physician before using it on infants, young children, or during pregnancy. Home Care and Lifestyle Tips to Prevent Fungal Recurrence Clearing up a fungal infection with cream is only half the battle. Fungi love warm, damp environments, and if you don't change the conditions that allowed them to grow in the first place, the infection can easily return. Here are simple, medically proven ways to keep your skin clear for good: Keep affected areas clean and completely dry: Fungi thrive in moisture. After showering or bathing, gently pat your skin dry with a clean towel instead of rubbing. Pay extra attention to skin folds, between your toes, and under the breasts. Never reuse wet or damp towels: Use a fresh, clean towel every time you dry off, and avoid sharing towels, clothes, or bedsheets with anyone else. Wash your towels in warm or hot water to help clear away any lingering fungal spores. Wear breathable, moisture-wicking fabrics: Choose loose-fitting clothing made of natural fibers like cotton, or moisture-wicking synthetic fabrics that draw sweat away from your skin. Change out of sweaty gym clothes or wet swimwear as soon as you are done working out or swimming. Practice smart footwear habits: Rotate your shoes so each pair has at least 24 hours to air out and dry completely before you wear them again. Wear clean, breathable cotton or wool socks, and change them during the day if your feet get sweaty. Protect your feet in public spaces: Always wear shower shoes, flip-flops, or sandals in high-risk areas like public gym showers, locker rooms, pool decks, and hotel bathrooms to avoid picking up fungal spores from the floor. Complete your full course of treatment: Even if the itching stops and your skin looks completely clear, keep using your antifungal cream for as long as your doctor or the product package instructs. Stopping treatment early can leave behind a few surviving fungal spores, leading to a quick recurrence. Keep your pets checked: If you have dogs or cats showing signs of hair loss, scaly patches, or itching, have a veterinarian check them for ringworm, as pets can easily pass fungal infections back to humans. How to Apply Antifungal Creams for Maximum Results Applying an antifungal cream correctly is just as important as choosing the right active ingredient. To make sure the medication works efficiently and clears the infection completely, follow these simple, physician-recommended steps: Clean and dry the area first: Gently wash the affected skin with mild soap and warm water to remove surface oils and dead skin cells. Pat the area completely dry with a clean towel instead of rubbing. Fungi thrive in moisture, so ensuring the skin, especially between toes or in skin folds, is entirely dry allows the cream to absorb properly. Apply beyond the visible border: Spread a thin, even layer of cream over the lesion and extend it roughly 1 to 2 centimeters (about half an inch to an inch) onto the healthy-looking skin around the edge of the rash. Microscopic fungal elements often spread into surrounding tissue before a visible rash forms, so treating this outer border prevents the infection from expanding. Complete the full treatment course: Stick to the duration printed on the product label or advised by your doctor. Even if the redness, scaling, and itching clear up within a few days, microscopic spores can survive under the skin surface. Continuing the application, often for 1 to 2 weeks after visible symptoms disappear, helps ensure the fungus is eradicated and significantly reduces the risk of a relapse. Wash your hands immediately after: Unless you are treating a fungal infection on your hands, wash them thoroughly with soap and water after applying the cream. This simple step prevents you from accidentally transferring fungal spores to other parts of your body or spreading them to others. Final Thought: Treating Fungal Infections Effectively When managed correctly, most superficial fungal infections are easily treatable with the right cream and a consistent routine. However, misidentifying a rash or applying the wrong product can turn a minor issue into a severe, widespread skin problem. To keep your skin healthy and clear, focus on proper application techniques, give your treatment time to work, and always consult a dermatologist before introducing unverified home remedies, as improper treatments can irritate damaged skin and make the infection worse.

body_text: Reports Improved Profitability and Early Momentum Following Archenia Acquisition SEATTLE, Aug. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Marchex, Inc. (NASDAQ: MCHX), a vertically focused, AI-driven conversation analytics, customer acquisition and optimization company, today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Marchex Q2 2026 Financial Highlights Revenue was $11.0 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $11.7 million for the second quarter of 2025. Net loss was $0.4 million or $(0.01) per diluted share for the second quarter of 2026, compared with net income of $0.1 million or $0.00 per diluted share for the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ("EBITDA") was $0.7 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $0.6 million for the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA includes $1.0 million of reorganization and acquisition-related costs. Adjusted EBITDA before those costs was $1.7 million. Adjusted non-GAAP income per share was $0.00 for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $0.02 for the second quarter of 2025. Pro Forma Combined Marchex and Archenia 2026 Financial Highlights Because the acquisition closed on July 1, 2026, Marchex’s reported second-quarter results do not include Archenia. The following supplemental unaudited pro forma results present the companies on a combined basis for the periods shown. For the first quarter of 2026, pro forma combined Revenue was $14.4 million and Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $0.1 million, which includes $0.7 million of reorganization and acquisition-related costs. Adjusted EBITDA before those costs was $0.6 million. For the second quarter of 2026, pro forma combined Revenue was $15.5 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $1.0 million, including $1.0 million of reorganization and acquisition-related costs. Adjusted EBITDA before those costs was $2.0 million. “The acquisition of Archenia advances our strategy of extending Marchex’s conversational intelligence capabilities from insights to actions and measurable outcomes,” said Russell Horowitz, Chairman of Marchex. “By combining our first-party conversational data and analytics with Archenia’s customer-qualification and acquisition technology, we can deliver greater value to customers while expanding our revenue opportunities. While we operate in a rapidly evolving and dynamic industry with uncertainties and various risks, we believe that the combined company can achieve greater revenue scale and growth, higher margins, expanded market reach, and enhanced strategic flexibility. Early customer adoption is encouraging and based on this, we plan to make selective investments in incremental sales and product development to support our 2027 growth opportunities.” Financial Outlook THE FOLLOWING FORWARD-LOOKING LOOKING STATEMENTS REFLECT MARCHEX’S EXPECTATIONS AS OF AUGUST 12, 2026 The Company currently anticipates that pro forma combined financial results for the three months ending September 30, 2026 will be in the range of (in millions): First Quarter 2026 (actual) Second Quarter 2026 (actual) Third Quarter 2026 (outlook) Revenue $14.4 $15.5 $16.0 - $16.5 Adjusted EBITDA, net of reorganization and acquisition costs $0.6 $2.0 $2.3 - $2.5 Marchex will provide its Fourth Quarter 2026 Financial Outlook and initial 2027 business outlook when it reports its Third Quarter 2026 Financial results, currently anticipated in early November 2026. Customer, Product, and New Growth Opportunities Updates Marchex and Archenia have been jointly developing and selling new solutions combining the capabilities of the companies. These offerings leverage Marchex’s data and AI signals with Archenia’s AI tool sets and user interface, including AI-verified outcomes, which drive increased revenue on a Pay-Per-Event basis, and Conversational AI Agents, which help increase customer bookings and appointment rates. Marchex believes its ability to sell these and other combined solutions, which reflect the bundling of insights, actions and outcomes, to its installed customer base will be a meaningful sales catalyst in 2026 and beyond. In May 2026, Marchex shared that its top 100 customers represent approximately 90% of its revenue, and this customer base has been the initial focus for presenting the products which leverage the combined capabilities of the companies. At that time, Marchex had made presentations to nearly one third of these customers, approximately half of whom have already purchased one or more of these products on a recurring or paid pilot basis. Of those remaining, Marchex stated that it believes that over time, the majority are also likely to purchase one or more of these products on a recurring or paid pilot basis. Since this time, the company has continued to see further progress and validation with these efforts. Examples of recent, successful sales of combined products to existing customers include: (1) An existing home services client, representing approximately $500,000 in annualized analytics revenue, adopted Archenia’s AI-verified outcomes, increasing total annualized revenue from the customer to more than $1 million. (2) An existing auto services customer, representing more than $300,000 in annualized analytics revenue, adopted a paid pilot program to improve sales agent behaviors at 40 retail locations, since expanding to more than 60 locations. This customer operates thousands of retail locations and if the pilot is converted into broader adoption, Marchex believes the customer can represent $1 million or more in annualized revenue. (3) An existing advertising/media customer, representing approximately $400,000 in annualized analytics revenue, launched a paid pilot program using the Marchex’s Conversational AI Agent to improve call handling. If the pilot is converted, Marchex believes the program could contribute incremental revenue in 2026 as well as increase annualized revenue from this customer by 50% or more in 2027. Archenia Transaction Update On July 1, 2026, the Company consummated the previously-announced acquisition of Archenia. Marchex’s acquisition of Archenia creates a vertically focused, AI-driven customer acquisition and outcome-optimization platform. Marchex brings a deep foundation of first-party data, derived from years of analyzing customer conversations for many industry-leading companies, with Archenia adding AI-powered lead qualification, conversational IVR, performance marketing infrastructure, and expertise in activating call intelligence at scale. Together, the companies provide a comprehensive platform that connects customer insights, automated actions, and measurable business outcomes. About Marchex Marchex and Archenia together harness proprietary AI-powered conversational intelligence and advanced customer acquisition technologies to transform consumer intent into actionable, outcome-driven business results. The combination of Marchex's prescriptive analytics and omnichannel intelligence with Archenia's AI-verified qualification, natural-language analytics, and automated decisioning capabilities creates a highly differentiated customer acquisition and optimization technology platform. Leveraging real-time AI signals, machine-learning models, and deep vertical market expertise, the company identifies consumer intent, improves qualification accuracy, and delivers verified outcomes such as high-intent conversations, appointments, and sales. Serving market leading companies across major verticals including automotive, insurance, home services, healthcare, and advertising/media, Marchex empowers organizations to optimize customer engagement and drive revenue growth through AI-driven insights, actions, and outcomes. Please visit www.marchex.com , www.marchex.com/blog , or @marchex on X, where Marchex discloses material information from time to time about the Company, its financial information, and its business. Non-GAAP Financial Information To supplement Marchex's consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP and to provide clarity internally and externally, Marchex uses certain non-GAAP measures of financial performance and liquidity, including adjusted EBITDA and adjusted non-GAAP income (loss) per share. Financial analysts and investors may use adjusted EBITDA to help with comparative financial evaluation to make informed investment decisions. Financial analysts and investors may use adjusted non-GAAP income (loss) per share to analyze Marchex's financial performance since these groups have historically used earnings per share related measures, along with other measures, to estimate the value of a Company, to make informed investment decisions, and to evaluate a Company's operating performance compared to that of other companies in its industry. Adjusted EBITDA represents net income (loss) before (1) interest, (2) income taxes, (3) amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions, (4) depreciation and amortization, (5) stock-based compensation expense, and (6) acquisition and disposition-related costs. Adjusted EBITDA is a metric by which Marchex has evaluated the performance of its business, to include being the basis on which Marchex's internal budgets have been based and by which Marchex's management has been evaluated. This measure is used by our management to understand and evaluate our core operating performance and trends, and management believes it provides meaningful information regarding the Company's liquidity and ability to fund its operations and financing obligations. Adjusted non-GAAP income (loss) per share represents adjusted non-GAAP income (loss) divided by GAAP diluted shares outstanding. Adjusted non-GAAP income (loss) generally captures those items on the statement of operations that have been, or ultimately will be, settled in cash exclusive of certain items that are not indicative of Marchex’s recurring core operating results and represents net income (loss) applicable to common stockholders plus the net of tax effects of: (1) stock-based compensation expense, (2) acquisition and disposition related costs, (3) amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions, and (4) interest (income) expense and other, net. Marchex's management believes that investors should have access to, and Marchex is obligated to provide, the same set of tools that management uses in analyzing the Company's results. These non-GAAP measures should be considered in addition to results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and should not be considered in isolation, as a substitute for, or superior to, GAAP results. Marchex’s non-GAAP financial measures may be defined differently from time to time and may be defined differently than similar titled terms used by other companies, and accordingly, care should be exercised in understanding how Marchex defines its non-GAAP financial measures in this release. Marchex endeavors to compensate for the limitations of the non-GAAP measures presented by providing the comparable GAAP measure with equal or greater prominence, GAAP financial statements, and detailed descriptions of the reconciling items and adjustments, including quantifying such items, to derive the non-GAAP measure. title: START: Chloe Sow, Co-Founder, Infera "The operating system for your laboratory”
summary: START: Chloe Sow, Co-Founder, Infera "The operating system for your laboratory”
body_text: Listen on Apple Podcasts Listen on Spotify Watch on YouTube Subscribe to START ‍ ‍ Scientific discovery shouldn't slow down because of software. But every instrument in the lab ships its own, and someone has to learn all of them. Researchers don't want to memorize instrument interfaces. They want experiments to run. They want answers. They want data. That's the problem Infera is solving. Chloe Sow knows that side of it. Mechanical engineering at Harvard, research at Brigham and Women's, building medical devices and running the experiments by hand. Her co-founder Troy Cheng spent an entire research summer figuring out how to run his lab's experiments on one machine. That was the summer. So they built the thing they needed. Describe an experiment in plain English. Infera turns it into a validated, instrument-ready run across the equipment your lab already uses. One system for protocol logic. Vendor-specific scripts. Laboratory data. Inventory. Institutional knowledge. Today, running an experiment means going instrument by instrument. Tomorrow, one place for all of them. AI agents already design experiments and protocols. But nothing connects those designs to real laboratory instruments. One system. From intent to execution.‍ Infera: "Control lab instruments with natural language" ‍ 🎙️ Chloe Sow , Co-Founder, Infera on Fondo START pod 00:45 Claude Code for scientific instruments 01:27 Troy's entire job was one liquid handler 02:39 Every run captures a record. The missing layer between AI and instruments 03:12 Scientists pressing buttons without knowing the machine 04:22 Plain English to validated instrument-ready run.
